title: Revolutionary
summary: Move the rook far enough sideways to keep promotion supported and skewer the king if the pawn is captured.

nodes.question: Can the rook leave the promotion square safely?
nodes.explanation: Black’s rook sits behind b7. White needs a rook move that both supports b8 and exploits the king on f7.

branches.title: Keep the pawn defended from h8
commentary: Begin after ...Rb1. The earlier eight-piece double-rook battle and rook sacrifice remain source context.
Rh8 is the only winning move in this exact five-piece position. It supports b8 across the eighth rank and prepares a skewer if the pawn disappears.
Rxb7 accepts the pawn, placing the rook behind its own king on the seventh rank.
Rh7+ checks Kf7, with Rb7 farther along the same rank. The king cannot capture the checking rook on h7 from f7.
Ke6 is the illustrated king retreat, exposing the rook on b7.
Rxb7 captures that rook. White reaches a checked king-and-rook win.
branches.explanation: Rxb7 captures that rook. White reaches a checked king-and-rook win.

branches.title: Choose a nearby rook square instead
commentary: This independent comparison tests why a generic sideways rook move is insufficient.
Ra8 gives away the win. The rook is now too close to the pawn’s file for the same seventh-rank skewer.
Rxb7 wins the pawn. Ra7 would attack the rook first, so that rook blocks the check against Kf7 and can move away. The exact remaining rook ending is drawn.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Rxb7 wins the pawn. Ra7 would attack the rook first, so that rook blocks the check against Kf7 and can move away. The exact remaining rook ending is drawn.

branches.title: Sacrifice the rook with an unprepared check
commentary: Another independent attempt tries to clear b8 with check, but must calculate the capture on the promotion file.
Rf8+ loses. Black’s king can capture the unprotected checking rook.
Kxf8 accepts that sacrifice. The pawn still cannot promote safely against Rb1.
b8=Q+ promotes with check, but the new queen is directly above the black rook.
Rxb8 captures the queen and removes the check. Black has a rook against the bare king and a checked win.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Rxb8 captures the queen and removes the check. Black has a rook against the bare king and a checked win.

exercises.prompt: Why does h8 work where a8 fails?
exercises.answer: After ...Rxb7, Rh7+ attacks the king first and the rook behind it. From a7, Black’s rook is the first piece hit and can move without exposing a check.

exercises.prompt: Why does the promotion with check still fail after Rf8+?
exercises.answer: A check can be answered by capture. The rook on b1 still has a clear path to b8 and can take the new queen.

startContext: Begin at the saved five-piece position after ...Rb1 at 137 seconds, following the earlier exchanges and capture of Black’s f-pawn. Only this final skewer and explicitly labeled independent errors are verified here.
